issues_detected.description: Series version numbering is non-monotonic: the current June 2026 release is 'Version 2.0' while the earlier October 2025 and June 2025 releases are each listed as 'Version 2.1' in version_access.versions_available. version_details explains that each quarterly release is a separate Dataverse dataset with its own version counter, but a reader comparing the list can misread 2.1 as newer than 2.0.
issues_detected.recommendation: State per entry that version numbers are repository-internal to each release DOI, or order the versions_available list explicitly by release date.

issues_detected.description: distribution_formats[1].access_urls 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/' is the Data Access API base path, not a resolvable URL; a datafile id must be appended. The format text does explain it as the programmatic route for archives above the web download limit.
issues_detected.recommendation: Describe the id-appending pattern in the format text and keep the release landing page (already in distribution_formats[0].access_urls) as the primary access URL.

issues_detected.description: Keyword list carries 'mass spectroscopy' (source term) where the technique is mass spectrometry, and the citation author list contains 'Ballllosero Navarro F', a likely source transcription artifact; both appear to be faithful transcriptions from the bundle.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add 'mass spectrometry' as a keyword alongside the verbatim source term and verify the author spelling against the live Dataverse citation.

issues_detected.description: publisher and last_updated_on are omitted although the citation names 'University of Virginia Dataverse' and maintainers records the UVA Dataverse (LibraData) as archival host; the omission is disclosed in source_caveats ('The bundle names no publisher for the release') rather than silent.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record publisher as University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData) on the strength of the citation string, keeping the caveat about the bundle gap.

issues_detected.description: preprocessing_strategies and labeling_strategies describe the MuSIC cell-map pipeline (node2vec, HPA image embedding, contrastive co-embedding, community detection, GO/Reactome + LLM annotation) while the release states computed cell maps are not included; every affected entry carries a source_caveat saying the step was not applied to the distributed artifacts, so the fields document a declared method for outputs not in the described holdings.
issues_detected.recommendation: Keep the entries with their caveats; when cell maps ship, attach this documentation to the distributed files and add the released input streams' own processing steps.

issues_detected.description: No errata field exists although source_caveats document that the three June 2026 immunofluorescence image archives report the same file sizes as the October 2025 ones but different MD5 checksums (regenerated archives) with no repository erratum explaining the regeneration, and the record consequently withholds the per-file protein counts.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record the observed regeneration as an errata/updates entry so the change is a first-class statement rather than a caveat.

issues_detected.description: Most of the 47 creators carry their institutional affiliation only as prose in notes; only the five University of Virginia authors (whose Dataverse listing prints a ROR URL) use the structured affiliations slot, so affiliation is not machine-readable for the rest.
issues_detected.recommendation: Promote the institution names in notes to structured affiliations entries with ROR identifiers where resolvable.

semantic_insights: Top-level identifiers agree end to end: id doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, doi 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, the citation DOI, page persistentId and version_access.latest_version_doi all name the same June 2026 release; DOI prefixes are correct for their registrars (10.18130 UVA Dataverse/LibraData, 10.1101 bioRxiv, 10.1038 Nature).

Grant identifiers are valid and correctly stratified: full award string '1OT2OD032742-01', core project 'OT2OD032742' with supplement '3OT2OD032742-01S2' and PI/period/amount from NIH RePORTER, and Bridge Center award '5U54HG012513-02' all follow NIH patterns.

RRIDs 'RRID:CVCL_0419' (MDA-MB-468) and 'RRID:CVCL_B5P3' (KOLF2.1J) use the Cellosaurus namespace correctly; ORCIDs are well-formed; nine authors without ORCIDs receive disclosed fragment identifiers minted on the release DOI rather than fabricated identifiers.

Human-subjects logic is internally consistent: involves_human_subjects=false, direct_collection.is_direct=false with explanation (commercial cell lines from ATCC and HipSci), is_deidentified with rationale ('cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject'), sensitive_elements_present=false with reasons, confidentiality_level 'unrestricted', and no consent or compensation claimed.

License logic is consistent across fields: license 'CC BY-NC-SA 4.0', license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission 'no_commercial_use', prohibited_uses restating the non-commercial and ShareAlike terms, and ip_restrictions naming the copyright holders (UC Regents, Stanford) who negotiate commercial licences under Data Access Committee supervision.

Temporal ordering is coherent: award start 2022-09-01, data creation 2025-02-27, release publication 2026-06-17, image archives 2026-07-15, award end 2026-08-31, quarterly augmentation through November 2026; the portal's conflicting 'Released on: June 17, 2025' is resolved against the higher-ranked Dataverse record with the resolution recorded in distribution_dates.source_caveats.

related_datasets and version_access tell the same story: four prior releases appear both as typed is_new_version_of relations and as versions_available entries, the Nature U2OS study is typed 'references' with an explicit note that it is a separate study, and the uncertain May 2024/DXWOS5 association is disclosed rather than asserted.

Source conflicts are resolved by declared source ranking in source_caveats (dates, 563 vs 464 imaged proteins, SRA links vs embargo, AP-MS 'coming soon' vs shipped), including the decision not to carry protein counts onto regenerated archives whose checksums changed — the record refuses to assert what its evidence cannot support.

Project-wide portal totals (1,374 interactions, 53,788 images, 7,023 proteins, 11,739 genes, 21.4 TB) are quarantined in notes with an explicit scope warning, and the one figure that also holds at release scope (11,739 genes) is identified as such.

correctness_validations.url_validity: all well-formed; one access_urls entry is an API base path requiring a datafile id

questions.description: Known biases with standard taxonomy and fairness analysis

questions.quality_note: Biases are categorized with enum-style taxonomy values, tied to affected subsets, and one carries a mitigation — clearly above the basic-identification anchor. The 5-point anchor is not reached: no AIO/CROISSANT RAI term mappings and no fairness or representativeness analysis.

strengths: Release-scoped identification and versioning done right: top-level id, doi, citation, page and latest_version_doi all name the June 2026 release, with version '2.0' and a typed is_new_version_of chain to all four prior releases.
Complete, correctly formatted identifiers and funding: stratified NIH award/core/supplement numbers, 38 ORCIDs plus disclosed minted ids, ROR, Cellosaurus RRIDs and correct DOI registrars throughout.
Per-modality collection documentation with reagents, instruments and scale, collectors assigned to all four data streams, bounded timeframes, and raw-data provenance to MassIVE/ATCC/HipSci.

Unusually complete use guidance: intended, discouraged and prohibited uses all populated, five typed limitations, two typed biases with a mitigation, structured missing-data documentation and specific foreseeable-misuse identification.

Rigorous source hygiene: conflicting dates, protein counts, embargo states and the regenerated image archives are resolved by declared source ranking in source_caveats, with unverifiable counts withheld rather than guessed.
weaknesses: Data-level file formats inside the ZIP archives are never named and no variables are described, so interoperability and file-type variety are assessable only at the packaging layer.

No errata field although the record itself observes silently regenerated image archives (same sizes, different MD5 checksums), and the publisher and last_updated_on slots are empty (disclosed bundle gaps).
Software tools carry URLs but no version numbers, and the preprocessing/labeling strategies describe the downstream cell-map pipeline rather than processing applied to the released input streams.
Treatment and differentiation conditions are not modelled as subpopulations or splits with counts, and no reidentification-risk statement covers the donor-derived genome-scale sequencing data.
Bias documentation lacks AIO/CROISSANT RAI term mappings and any quantitative fairness analysis; most creator affiliations are prose notes rather than structured entries.
recommendations: Name the payload formats per archive (e.g. TIFF/PNG images, mzML/RAW mass spectrometry, FASTQ/h5ad perturb-seq) in file_collections and add variables for the principal data tables.
Record the June 2026 image-archive regeneration as an errata entry, populate publisher with University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData), and add structured total_size_bytes per collection.
Record tool versions for the Cell Mapping Toolkit, FAIRSCAPE, node2vec and IMP, and document the processing actually applied to the released input streams alongside the caveated MuSIC pipeline.
Model the treatment/differentiation conditions as subpopulations or subsets with counts, and add a reidentification-risk statement for the KOLF2.1J donor-derived sequencing data.
Map the two known_biases entries to AIO terms, add a coverage-bias entry for the incomplete modality overlap, and promote creator affiliations from notes prose to structured entries.
